final.investment_thesis:
The risk debate was genuinely balanced on the question that matters — whether to hold a 2% claim on upside optionality or step aside — and the deciding evidence favors retaining it at exactly this size rather than adding or exiting. What is not in dispute across any seat: FQ3 FY26 revenue +16.4%, gross margin 50.06%, diluted EPS +28.7%, 9M FCF +52.5% and $62.2B net cash, with price 314.58 trading 11.4% above a rising 200-SMA at 282.35, MACD histogram positive on 8/26, the 300–302.79 shelf defended four times, and VWMA at 309.10 still 1.77% below spot. That fortress and intact primary trend is why this is not Sell and why the aggressive analyst is right that a 0% allocation abandons a real claim for a fee. Nor is the hostile side disputed: 34.3x on roughly a $9.17 annualized run-rate means 30x is −12.6% and 25x is −27.2%; 317–320 was rejected on 8/19 and 8/20, and the advance since has come on roughly 35M shares versus the 50.5M topping day and the 132.5M-share −7.35% gap of 7/31 whose cause is still unexplained in the supplied record; current deferred revenue is +5.3% against +16% revenue, opex grew +22.9% faster than revenue, inventory is $11.1B versus $5.7B, and the buyback was cut to 67% of FCF — removing the share-count mechanism that supported the premium. A 300.37 stop is 0.43–2x ATR in a name that gapped 7.35% in one session, so it is narrative, not protection.

Sizing resolves the disagreement. The aggressive analyst's framing of the 2% as a cheap option is directionally right but overstates it: at 2%, a 6–9.5% squeeze to 333.43/344.57 adds only about 0.12–0.19% of total equity, while a 13–27% multiple reset costs about 0.26–0.55% and a 4.5% stop about 0.09%. The conservative analyst is right that unconfirmed participation still carries event drawdown, but wrong to imply the stub should be treated as zero-value until confirmation — nothing in the supplied evidence justifies paying roughly $2 in fees to liquidate 6.4 shares and give up a dated binary catalyst with 98% of the account already idle in non-interest-bearing cash. The neutral analyst's symmetry call is the correct synthesis: no add, no trim, hold the measured 2.02%. Critically, the retention is justified independently today — 2.02% survives a fresh total-exposure assessment on its own merits — not by mechanically discounting yesterday's position again; there is no fresh justification for another proportional trim, and repeated trimming without a new total-target rationale would be exactly the error the past AAPL record punishes (the 06-30 through 07-24 and 08-13 Underweights each gave up 3–9% of five-day alpha by trimming inside an intact uptrend).

What would change it: a daily close above 317.04 on >50M shares followed by a close above 320.28 with MACD reclaiming zero and RSI >60 would break the two-rejection pattern and justify paying up for evidence toward a 4–5% total target, with 333.43 and 340.08 as upside references. Conversely a daily close below 309.10–311.50 breaks the fused 10-EMA/50-SMA/VWMA cluster and validates the bear case, and a close below 300.37/300.00 invalidates the base entirely — either is a reason to cut to 0%, not to average down. The late-October FQ4 print must also show gross margin ≥49.5% with the $11.1B inventory absorbed, and the FY26 10-K must source the $13.3B intangible against the matched $13.5B noncurrent liability. Stated gaps, not papered over: no entry price was provided, no portfolio-level constraints or tax lot detail are given (so sizing here is against total account equity in this single-stock cash simulation), the 8/20–8/24 news window and insider data are unavailable, no options chain or implied volatility exists to price any hedge, and the cause of the 7/31 gap remains unestablished — so all levels are technical, not valuation-derived, and stops/limits are narrative conditions only, never placed orders.
